display.purpose: Space Grotesk — CTA buttons and marketing/brand moments only. Never in-app labels or page titles.

body.purpose: Inter at 0.75rem — the workhorse for UI text and most prose. Prose caps at 65–75ch.

mono.purpose: source-code-pro — literal data: key=value label sets, IDs, query values, log/ANSI output.

shadows.name: ring-card
shadows.purpose: The only in-shell elevation — a translucent hairline ring etching cards/panels into the dark. Not a drop shadow.

motion.name: ease-expo-out
motion.purpose: The universal control easing for hover/focus/state transitions, at 200ms.

motion.name: ease-reveal
motion.purpose: Fade-up entrance for content reveals (0.7s); used sparingly, never as a page-load sequence.

motion.name: duration-control
motion.purpose: Standard transition duration across interactive components.

narrative.overview: Everr's interface is a precision readout for software delivery: dark, dense, and calm at rest, with the lime accent lighting up only what is live, selected, or actionable. It looks like a tool built to be watched under load — legible when the data is thick, fast when the user is mid-incident, quiet when nothing demands attention. Depth is implied by tonal layering and a single hairline ring, not by shadow. It practices what Everr preaches: an observability tool's own UI must feel instrumented-grade — no sloppy states, no decorative motion, no chrome between the user and the runtime fact. It rejects the legacy enterprise wall-of-dashboards, the generic shadcn SaaS template, consumer-y over-animation, and AI-gimmick flourishes.
keyCharacteristics: Dark-first, near-black base with tonally-layered panels — depth without shadows.
A single chartreuse accent (Signal Lime) reserved for live / selected / actionable state.
Dense, compact controls (32px default height) tuned for expert throughput.
One consistent interaction signature: dotted focus outline + lime focus ring, expo-out easing.
Inter for everything functional; Space Grotesk reserved for CTA and marketing display.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Lime marks what is live, selected, or actionable — never decoration. Its scarcity is what makes it read as signal.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth is tonal, not cast. Panels lift by stepping lightness and a single hairline ring. Drop shadows are prohibited in the app shell.

rules.name: The Status-Plus-Shape Rule
rules.body: Status never rides on color alone. Pair red/lime/muted with an icon, badge label, or shape so firing/pending/inactive survive colorblind viewing.

rules.name: The Fixed-Scale Rule
rules.body: App typography is a fixed rem scale, never clamp(). A heading that shrinks inside a sidebar looks worse, not better.

rules.name: The Space-Grotesk-Is-A-Guest Rule
rules.body: The display face appears on CTAs and brand surfaces only. Using it for in-app labels, data, or page titles breaks the tool-disappears-into-the-task contract.

rules.name: The Ring-Not-Border Rule
rules.body: Containers separate from their background with a translucent hairline ring (ring-1 ring-foreground/10), not an opaque border and never a colored stripe.

dos: Do reserve Signal Lime for live / selected / actionable state — when it appears, it must mean something.
Do convey depth with tonal layering and a ring-1 ring-foreground/10 hairline — never a drop shadow in the content plane.
Do keep the one interaction signature on every control: h-8 default, rounded-md, dotted focus outline → 2px lime ring at 3px offset, cubic-bezier(0.19,1,0.22,1) at 200ms.
Do pair status color with a label, icon, or shape.
Do use Inter for everything functional and a fixed rem type scale; keep muted text legible, not faint.
Do embrace density where experts need it while keeping rows readable.
Do use skeleton loaders and teaching empty states, not mid-content spinners or 'nothing here.'
donts: Don't ship the generic shadcn SaaS template look — untouched card-grid-of-everything, rounded-everything, gradient accents.
Don't build the legacy enterprise observability wall — cramped chrome, a thousand knobs, dashboards you can look at but never query.
Don't add consumer-y over-animation — no bounce, no elastic, no decorative gradients, no choreographed page-load sequences.
Don't ship AI-gimmick flourishes — no sparkles badging, no mascot, no chatbot bolted onto the chrome.
Don't use Space Grotesk for in-app labels, data, or page titles — it's a guest, reserved for CTA/brand.
Don't use border-left/border-right > 1px as a colored accent stripe, gradient text, or glassmorphism as default.
Don't spend Signal Lime on inactive states, decorative fills, or large surfaces.
Don't use clamp() fluid type or drop shadows inside the app shell.
